两版分别走“取票，再领蓝”，最终多少分？
有效果版走“领蓝，再等待”，能否在结束时再次拿票？
有效果版送件后，邮票套组还得4分吗？
答案：第一题基础版有2张票券，加套组4分，共6分；效果版领蓝时再拿1张，共7分。第二题不能再次触发，结果是套组4分加2张票券，共6分。第三题仍得4分，因为费用只交票券；“领蓝，再送件”合计9分。
来源与范围

Geoffrey Engelstein 与 Isaac Shalev，Building Blocks of Tabletop Game Design，第二版，SET-01 “Set Valuation”（印刷页509—512）讨论集合的利益与估值曲线；SET-05 “Combo Abilities”（523—525）讨论能力之间的协同、取得与运作，并区分宽泛的收集现象和具体机制。本站用“估值—触发—后续动作”组织以上对照；全部邮票规则与数字均为原创，不是书中的练习，也没有将一次写明的触发链等同于作者讨论的全部组合玩法。
After completing a set: connecting points and effects

Collecting the required symbols can score at the end or immediately change what you can do next. Both relationships can exist in the same design. To compare them, specify what forms a set, what it is worth, and whether completing it triggers another effect.
Two actions at the stamp window

This original example is a single-player local phase with all information public. You start with one red stamp, one ticket, and zero points. The supply holds one blue stamp and three tickets. Stamps and tickets are different objects. Take exactly two actions, each chosen from the legal options below. You may repeat an action if it remains legal.
Action · Requirement and result
Take the blue stamp · If it remains in the supply, take it for free; there is only one in this phase
Take a ticket · If the supply has at least one ticket, take one for free
Deliver a parcel · If you hold at least two tickets and have not delivered in this phase, return two tickets to the supply and immediately score 5 points
Wait · Always legal; changes no objects or points

There are no other actions, trades, discards, or sources of objects. End the phase after resolving the second action and all its effects. Holding one red and one blue stamp scores 4 points once; a lone stamp scores nothing. Keep the stamps rather than returning them. Each remaining ticket scores 1 additional point. With one player, simply record the final score; there is no separate win condition or next round.
In the base version, completing the stamp set has no immediate effect. The total of four tickets stays constant, split between you and the supply.
Resolve the base version first

Blue stamp, then ticket: The first action completes the red-blue set, but you still have only one ticket. The second action takes a ticket, leaving you with two. At the end, score 4 for the set and 2 for the tickets: 6 points.
Ticket, then delivery: After the first action you hold two tickets. Return both for the second action and score 5 points. You finish with only the red stamp, no set bonus, and no tickets: 5 points.
“Blue stamp, then delivery” is illegal in the base version: taking the stamp did not give you another ticket. The set's future 4 points cannot pay a cost that currently requires tickets.
Add only an effect for the first completion

Reset to the initial state. Add just this rule: When your red-blue set first becomes complete, immediately take one ticket from the supply without spending an action. Mark this effect as used for the phase; it cannot trigger again. If the supply is empty, take nothing but still mark the effect used. All other actions, the two-action length, the set's 4 points, and remaining-ticket scoring stay unchanged.

With this initial state and two-action limit, the supply always has a ticket when the set first completes. The empty-supply clause defines the effect's boundary; it does not introduce a third action or an extra starting state.

Repeat “blue stamp, then ticket.” Taking blue triggers a ticket, increasing your holding from one to two. Your second action takes another, leaving three. Score 4 for the set plus 3 for tickets: 7 points. With the same action sequence, the added effect increases the score by 1.

Another sequence is now legal: “blue stamp, then delivery.” The completion effect brings your tickets to two, enough to pay for delivery. Return both and score 5 immediately. You did not spend the stamps, so the completed set still scores 4 at the end: 9 points. The added effect supplies a resource and lets a later action meet its cost threshold.
Same initial state · Without a completion effect · With the first-completion effect
Blue stamp → ticket · 6 points · 7 points
Ticket → delivery · 5 points · 5 points
Blue stamp → delivery · Second action is illegal · 9 points

Neither version replaces “score 4 for the set” with “gain a ticket for the set.” The ticket is an additional effect; the points remain. Changing the reward type, timing, and consumption of the set together would obscure which rule produced the difference.
Separate valuation, triggering, and the next action

The valuation relationship is that red and blue together are worth 4 points. The trigger grants a ticket on first completion. The next connection is that tickets can pay for delivery. Delivery is not part of the automatic effect: you must still choose it as your second action. You can instead wait and let the extra ticket score 1 at the end.

This is a short, explicitly prescribed effect chain. It does not demonstrate players discovering and separately acquiring many abilities to assemble a complex combo, or a complete engine that can keep running. It establishes the narrower point that set rewards and connections between actions can coexist. For a fuller ability combination, open the related Combo building entry below.

Set valuation need not mean end-game points: a set can provide resources, immediate points, or other benefits. This example fixes it at 4 end-of-phase points to make the added trigger's effect visible. For different valuation curves, open the related Set Collection entry below.
Where the chain stops

Taking blue uses an action. The automatic ticket does not, but happens only once. Delivery still uses an action and is allowed only once. The phase ends after the second action resolves. Final scoring checks the set; it does not create another “first completion.” Spending tickets neither removes stamps nor completes the set again.

There is no infinite loop here because the specified object movements and trigger limits prevent repetition. If later abilities return stamps, reacquire them, or grant new actions after delivery, you must trace the triggers and stopping conditions again.

Nine exceeding six is a calculation for this fixed phase. It does not establish that the new effect makes a whole game more enjoyable or balanced, or always broadens choices. A stronger route may make other routes less appealing. In a real test, first record whether readers distinguish automatic effects from chosen actions, then observe whether they still have reasons to consider other routes.
Check yourself: what if you take a ticket first?
What scores result from “ticket, then blue stamp” in the two versions?
In the effect version, can “blue stamp, then wait” grant another ticket at final scoring?
Does the set still score 4 after delivery in the effect version?

Answers: For the first question, the base version ends with two tickets plus the set: 6 points. The effect version gains another ticket when blue arrives: 7 points. For the second, the effect cannot trigger again; score 4 for the set plus 2 for tickets, totaling 6. For the third, yes: the cost spends only tickets. “Blue stamp, then delivery” totals 9.
Sources and scope

Geoffrey Engelstein and Isaac Shalev, Building Blocks of Tabletop Game Design, second edition: SET-01, “Set Valuation” (printed pp. 509–512), discusses benefits and valuation curves; SET-05, “Combo Abilities” (pp. 523–525), discusses synergy, acquisition, and operation of abilities, distinguishing broad collecting patterns from specific mechanisms. The valuation–trigger–next-action comparison is our organization of this example. All stamp rules and numbers are original, not an exercise from the book; a single prescribed trigger chain does not represent the full range of combo play discussed by the authors.
区域里有人，就知道谁控制了吗？
“这块区域是我的”可能意味着你最后进入过、你的人数最多，或别人经过附近时受到限制。设计者需要把这些句子变成不同的判断。本页先在同一块共存棋盘上只改收益归属，再用一个独立的移动对照说明控制区。
固定棋盘与放置过程
这是本站原创的三人局部阶段，甲、乙、丙都从0分开始。北站值3分，南站值2分。各色影响子可以共存，不战斗、不移除，也不阻挡别人放置。两个站的初态如下：
站点 · 甲的影响子 · 乙的影响子 · 丙的影响子 · 记名标记
初始记名标记视为此前最后一次进入的记录，无须倒推此前的过程。每人另有1枚预备影响子。按甲、乙、丙顺序，每人只行动一次：免费把自己的预备子放进任一站，或等待。放置后，把该站记名标记改为放置者；等待不改标记。没有其他行动，未使用的预备子不计分。
丙行动结束后才结算两个站，之后阶段结束，不再放置。基础版把每站全部分数给该站记名者，不检查人数。每站最多有一个记名者；标记并不代表禁止别人共存。各自记分，总分并列就并列，不另设破同分规则。
第一条过程：同样投入，记名与人数不同
甲放北站，乙放南站，丙放北站。最终北站是甲3、乙1、丙1，记名丙；南站是甲0、乙2、丙1，记名乙。
基础版只看标记：丙得北站3分，乙得南站2分，结果为甲0、乙2、丙3。丙没有靠一枚子变成北站人数最多的人，只是成为最后放置者。
现在恢复同一初态，保持全部行动和标记更新不变，只改一句收益规则：每站分数给该站影响子数量唯一最多的人；最多人数并列，或全站无人，则该站无人得分。不分第二名，不分摊奖励。记名标记仍照常更新，但不参与这个版本的收益判断。
重复甲北、乙南、丙北。北站甲3枚，唯一最多，得3分；南站乙2枚，得2分。结果变成甲3、乙2、丙0。区域里的人、放置权限与行动顺序都没变，变的是用哪一种状态决定受益者。
第二条过程：全部投入北站
再从初态开始，这次甲、乙、丙都放北站。北站最终为3／2／1，记名丙；南站仍为0／1／1，记名乙。
记名版仍是甲0、乙2、丙3。人数版中，甲的3枚是北站唯一最多，得3分；南站乙丙各1枚，并列最多，无人得2分。结果为甲3、乙0、丙0。
固定动作顺序 · 北站最终人数：甲／乙／丙 · 南站最终人数：甲／乙／丙 · 记名版总分：甲／乙／丙 · 人数版总分：甲／乙／丙
第二条过程的北站共有6枚子，甲有3枚，没有超过总数的一半，但仍唯一最多。本例使用相对多数，不要求绝对过半。与此同时，南站已有影响子，也已有记名者，却在人数版没有受益者。“存在”“归谁记名”“谁拿收益”并不是同一个状态。
这次没有改占用权限
本例的记名制度只有一个受益者，但允许多方共存。它是为了隔离收益判断而设计的规则，不能直接当作所有“绝对控制”游戏的缩小模型。有些游戏不许敌方共存，进入就战斗；有些保留撤离后的归属；还有些在特定时点才变更控制。这些都需要另外写规则。
如果把记名版同时改成“不能放进别人的站”，第一条过程可能根本走不完。届时比较中既改了合法行动，也改了收益，不能再把分数变化全归因于人数计算。想研究排他占用，可继续读下方关联条目《区域控制》；想研究人数与平手，可读《区域多数》。
控制区是另一条移动规则
下面是独立的小型移动对照，不给上面的站点加入新能力。四个格子只通过三条双向边连接：西—桥、桥—东、桥—岗。信使起初在西，敌方守卫固定在岗，不行动。信使只走一次，每跨一条边花1移动力，最多花2点，可以提前停止，也可以原路返回；禁止进入岗，没有攻击、得分或其他效果。
基础移动规则下，选择路径西→桥→东，花2点，结束在东。只增加一条控制区规则：每次进入与敌方守卫所在格相邻的格子，立即结束这次移动，剩余移动力作废。仍想走同一路径时，进入桥就必须停止，结束在桥，剩余1点不能花，也不能在本次移动中返回西。
守卫没有站在桥上，却通过邻接关系限制了桥上的移动。这个限制没有自动给守卫桥的所有权、北站的收益或任何多数分数。这里的控制区只是“进入邻格就停步”；其他游戏可能改用额外费用、攻击或不同离开条件，不能从名称推定一律相同。
设计时分别问三个问题
谁能进入或共存，决定动作是否合法；依据哪个状态分配收益，决定谁拿到什么；单位能影响哪些邻格，决定它在所在格之外施加什么限制。三个问题可以连接，但连接本身必须由规则写出。
记名版在这两个给定过程中让最后投入者得北站奖励，不代表它在所有棋盘上都只有最后一手重要。人数版保留了早先投入的影响，也不自动意味着更公平。这里没有检验多轮顺序、不同放置费用或真人谈判；需要研究哪一项，就保持其余条件相同再比较。
自查：等待会擦掉什么？
三人都等待，两版分别怎样结算？
三人都放北站，人数版中丙是否可因最后放置而得3分？
移动对照启用控制区后，信使可以留在西吗？守卫因此拥有桥吗？
答案：第一题等待不改标记或人数。记名版为甲3、乙2、丙0；人数版北站甲唯一最多，南站乙丙并列，因此为甲3、乙0、丙0。第二题不能，最后放置不参与人数版计分。第三题可以在移动前就停止，留在西；桥没有定义所有权，不能凭控制区推导出归属。
来源与范围

Geoffrey Engelstein 与 Isaac Shalev，Building Blocks of Tabletop Game Design，第二版：ARC-01 “Absolute Control”（印刷页486—487）讨论单一归属、共存边界及撤离后的控制记录；ARC-02 “Area Majority/Influence”（488—490）讨论多方存在、收益与平手；ARC-07 “Zone of Control”（501—502）讨论单位通过附近空间影响移动或攻击。本页将归属、收益与移动分开检验；站点、记名制度和信使过程均为本站原创，未借用书中具体游戏的规则或将本站对照当作统一分类定义。
Does presence tell you who controls an area?

“This area is mine” might mean you entered it last, have the most pieces there, or constrain enemies passing nearby. A designer must turn those sentences into distinct rules. This page first changes only the beneficiary on a shared board, then uses a separate movement comparison to explain a zone of control.
Fix the board and placement procedure

This original local phase has three players, A, B, and C, starting at zero points. North Station is worth 3 points and South Station 2. Influence pieces of different colors coexist: they neither fight nor remove pieces, and do not block placement. The initial stations are:
Station · A's pieces · B's pieces · C's pieces · Registration marker
North · 2 · 1 · 0 · A
South · 0 · 1 · 1 · B

Treat the initial markers as records of the last entry before this phase; you need not reconstruct that history. Each player also has one reserve piece. In A–B–C order, each takes exactly one action: place their reserve piece in either station for free, or wait. Placement changes that station's registration marker to the player placing. Waiting does not change it. There are no other actions, and unused reserve pieces score nothing.

Score both stations only after C's action, then end the phase with no further placement. In the base version, a station's registered player receives its entire reward, regardless of piece counts. Each station has at most one registered player; registration does not prohibit coexistence. Record each player's score; equal total scores remain tied, with no further tiebreaker.
First sequence: the same investment gives different leaders
A places North, B South, and C North. North ends with A3, B1, C1 and C registered. South ends with A0, B2, C1 and B registered.

The base version checks only the markers: C receives North's 3 points and B South's 2. The result is A0, B2, C3. C's one piece did not become the largest force at North; C was simply the last player to place there.

Reset to the same initial state. Keep all actions and marker updates unchanged, altering just the reward rule: A station's points go to the player with uniquely the most influence pieces there. If the highest count is tied, or the station is empty, nobody scores there. There is no second-place reward or sharing. Continue updating registration markers, but they do not determine rewards in this version.

Repeat A North, B South, C North. A's three pieces are uniquely the most at North, earning 3. B's two earn 2 at South. The result becomes A3, B2, C0. Pieces, placement permissions, and turn order are unchanged; only the state used to select the beneficiary differs.
Second sequence: everyone invests in North
Start again from the initial state, with all three placing North. North ends at 3/2/1 with C registered; South remains 0/1/1 with B registered.

Registration scoring still gives A0, B2, C3. Under count-based scoring, A's three pieces are uniquely the most at North, earning 3. B and C tie at South with one each, so nobody receives its 2 points. The result is A3, B0, C0.
Fixed action sequence · Final North counts: A/B/C · Final South counts: A/B/C · Registration scores: A/B/C · Count-based scores: A/B/C
A North, B South, C North · 3/1/1 · 0/2/1 · 0/2/3 · 3/2/0

In the second sequence, North has six pieces. A holds three, not more than half, but still uniquely the most. This example uses a plurality rather than requiring an absolute majority. Meanwhile, South has pieces and a registered player yet no beneficiary under count-based scoring. Presence, registration, and receiving a reward are different states.
Occupancy permissions have not changed

The registration system here selects one beneficiary while allowing coexistence. It is a rule designed to isolate reward determination, not a miniature model of every absolute-control game. Some games prohibit enemy coexistence and start combat on entry; some preserve ownership after departure; others change control only at specified times. Each needs its own rules.

If you also change the registration version to prohibit placement in another player's station, the first sequence may no longer be playable. You would be changing legal actions as well as rewards, so could not attribute the score difference entirely to counting pieces. Open the related entries below: Area control for exclusive occupancy, and Area majority for counts and ties.
A zone of control is a separate movement rule

The following is an independent movement comparison, not a new ability added to the stations. Four spaces have only three two-way connections: West–Bridge, Bridge–East, and Bridge–Post. A courier starts at West. An enemy guard stays at Post and does not act. The courier makes one move, paying one movement point per edge, with a maximum of two points. It may stop early or retrace its path. Entering Post is forbidden. There are no attacks, scores, or other effects.

Under the base movement rule, choosing West→Bridge→East costs two points and ends at East. Add only this zone-of-control rule: Each time you enter a space adjacent to the enemy guard's space, immediately end this move and forfeit remaining movement points. Attempting the same route now stops at Bridge. The remaining point cannot be spent, including to return to West during this move.

The guard is not on Bridge but restricts movement there through adjacency. This restriction does not automatically give the guard ownership of Bridge, a station's income, or any majority points. Here the zone only means stopping on entry to an adjacent space. Other games may use extra costs, attacks, or different departure conditions; the name does not specify one universal rule.
Ask three separate design questions

Who can enter or coexist determines legal actions. Which state allocates a reward determines who receives what. Which nearby spaces a unit affects determines the restrictions it projects beyond its own location. You can connect these questions, but the rules must specify the connections.

Registration rewards the last contributor at North in these two sequences; that does not establish that only the last turn matters on every board. Count-based scoring preserves the effect of earlier investment without automatically being fairer. These examples do not test multiple rounds, different placement costs, or human negotiation. Select the next factor you want to study and keep other conditions fixed.
Check yourself: what does waiting erase?
How do the two versions score if everyone waits?
If everyone places North, can C claim its 3 points for placing last under count-based scoring?
With the zone-of-control rule active, may the courier stay at West? Does the guard own Bridge?

Answers: First, waiting changes neither markers nor counts. Registration gives A3, B2, C0. Under count-based scoring, A leads North while B and C tie South: A3, B0, C0. Second, no: placing last is not part of that scoring rule. Third, the courier may stop before moving and remain at West. No ownership of Bridge is defined, so it cannot be inferred from the zone of control.
Sources and scope

Geoffrey Engelstein and Isaac Shalev, Building Blocks of Tabletop Game Design, second edition: ARC-01, “Absolute Control” (printed pp. 486–487), discusses single ownership, coexistence boundaries, and control records after departure; ARC-02, “Area Majority/Influence” (pp. 488–490), discusses multiple players' presence, benefits, and ties; ARC-07, “Zone of Control” (pp. 501–502), discusses units affecting movement or attacks through nearby spaces. This page separately tests registration, rewards, and movement. The stations, registration procedure, and courier example are original; they neither reproduce the book's games nor prescribe a universal classification.
玩家淘汰：少了一枚棋子，还是少了一位参与者？
移走玩家的一枚棋子，不必然淘汰玩家；是否失去后续行动或竞争资格，要看具体触发规则。本页讨论退出参与的安排，并把触发淘汰、材料去向、等待区间和复归条件分别写清楚。
先说明退出的是什么
Geoffrey Engelstein 与 Isaac Shalev 的 VIC-08 “Player Elimination”以最后一位留下的玩家获胜为起点，也讨论退出后的等待，以及只在终局取消获胜资格的变体。这些安排不能互相代替：继续正常行动、只是最后无资格获胜，和中途失去所有行动，是不同后果。
下面的原创阶段有三轮上限，也可能提前只剩一位参赛者。失去最后一台站才会触发退出；台站数量与参赛资格各用一项记录。没有把等待换算为实测分钟。
三轮信号争夺
林、乔、沐依次行动，每轮各有一个行动名额，共三轮。起始台站数为林 2、乔 1、沐 2；每人有 2 电池、0 分。台站只是本例的棋子。所有信息公开，另放一个空的移除区和一个空的已用电池区。
有资格且仍有台站的玩家，每次任选一个行动：广播，得 2 分；干扰，先付 1 电池到已用区，移除任意一位对手的 1 台站；或等待，什么也不改变。干扰的目标必须仍有资格并至少有 1 台站，不能选自己，费用不足不能干扰。每次只移除一站。没有其他收入、交易、借用或补站。
原规则中，某人台站归零就立即失去本阶段参赛资格。以后直接跳过他的名额，不能再广播、干扰、花钱或替别人决定；没有临终反击。他已得的分数仍记在纸上，未花的电池留在本人处，但不能用于本阶段获胜。移除的台站按原主人放进移除区，不送给攻击者。
每次行动后检查：若仅剩一人有资格，阶段立即结束，由他获胜，不再补完三轮；否则完成三轮后，在仍有资格的人中比较分数，最高分者获胜，同分并列。淘汰者在本阶段不复归。阶段结果结清后，如果大家另开一段同样的试赛，所有人按初始状态重新加入；这不会改写刚才的结果。
过程一：第一步让乔退出
第一轮，林干扰乔，花 1 电池，乔唯一的台站被移除，立即退出。乔的第一轮名额跳过。沐广播，得 2 分。
第二轮，林广播，得 2 分；乔的名额继续跳过；沐干扰林，花 1 电池，林从两站剩一站，仍能参与。第三轮林广播再得 2 分，乔跳过，沐广播再得 2 分。
最后林与沐各 4 分，都是有资格的并列胜者；乔 0 分且无资格。台站剩 1／0／2，移除区有林、乔各一站；电池剩 1／2／1，已用区共 2 电池。五个台站、六个电池都有去向。
乔错过了自己的三个行动名额。在他退出后，别人实际作出五次选择：沐第一轮、林与沐第二轮、林与沐第三轮。这是五次选择，不是五分钟；一次选择要多久、乔如何看待等待，都需要另行观察。
过程二：保留乔的三次行动
重置初始状态，只把林第一轮的选择改为广播。林第二、三轮仍广播；沐仍按“广播、干扰林、广播”行动；乔只要能正常行动就广播。
第一轮三人各得 2 分。第二轮林与乔各再得 2 分，沐花 1 电池移除林的一站。第三轮三人都广播。结束时林 6 分、乔 6 分、沐 4 分，林与乔并列获胜。台站剩 1／1／2，移除区只有林的一站；电池剩 2／2／1，已用区有 1 电池。
乔没有遭到归零，获得了三次真实选择机会；这里将他每次选择固定为广播，以便完成对照。不能据此推断“淘汰总是有利”或“保留别人总是更好”：改变目标、分值或其他人的选择，结果还会变化。
只替换首次归零后的处理
仍采用过程一的行动计划，只替换一条退出规则：每人第一次台站归零时保留参赛资格，等待紧接的本人行动名额；这个名额只能从自己的移除区收回 1 台站，不付电池，也不广播或干扰。之后若再次归零，才按原规则永久退出。其余费用、顺序、三轮上限与获胜规则不变。等待复归时没有台站，不能成为干扰目标。
第一轮林仍移除乔的唯一台站。接下来乔用自己的名额复归到一站，得分仍为 0；沐广播。第二轮林广播，乔广播得 2 分，沐干扰林。第三轮三人广播。
结果林、乔、沐各 4 分，三人仍有资格，因此并列获胜。乔只失去第一次正常选择，第二、三轮可以自己决定行动。这次首次归零变成了暂时失去行动机会，不能再把它描述为整段退出。
若有人在本人最后一个名额之后才首次归零，不追加复归名额。三轮结束时，他仍保留资格，按既有分数参加比较；不能因为等待复归而延长阶段。
完整过程 · 最后台站：林／乔／沐 · 剩余电池 · 记录分数
复归版移除区只剩林的一站；乔那一站已归还，未凭空增加棋子。已用电池仍为 2。这个改法改变了归零后的参与状态，以及后续能取得的分数；算例没有证明哪种安排更受玩家欢迎。
自查：现在还能做什么？
林从两站减到一站，是否要跳过后续行动？不用。他仍有台站与参赛资格；棋子移除本身不是玩家淘汰。
原版乔退出后还有 2 电池，能再付一枚帮沐干扰吗？不能。保留材料不等于保留行动权，本例也没有转交或临终行动。
复归版乔第一轮收回台站后，能接着广播得 2 分吗？不能。复归已经用掉那个行动名额；他的第一次广播在第二轮。
若一次干扰后仅剩沐有资格，还要等第三轮结束吗？不用。立即结束，沐获胜；不能继续计算已经取消的后续名额。
来源与范围

核心来源为 Geoffrey Engelstein 与 Isaac Shalev，Building Blocks of Tabletop Game Design: An Encyclopedia of Mechanisms，第二版，CRC Press，2022，第 5 章 VIC-08 “Player Elimination”（EPUB 锚点 filepos500251）。已读完整描述与讨论。三轮试赛、材料、分值、行动计划和首次复归对照均为本站原创；轮数上限是本例选择，不是淘汰机制的必然条件。书目与 DOI
BGG 2685：Player Elimination 是相关分类身份参照。本页把具体退出与复归规则逐项写出，没有从标签补出规则，也不把脚本核算当作旁观体验测试。
Player elimination: one fewer piece, or one fewer participant?

Removing a player's piece does not necessarily eliminate the player. Losing subsequent actions or eligibility depends on the particular trigger rules. This entry examines departure from participation, specifying the elimination trigger, material destinations, waiting interval, and return conditions separately.
Specify what the player leaves

Geoffrey Engelstein and Isaac Shalev's VIC-08, “Player Elimination,” starts with the last remaining player winning. It also discusses waiting after removal and variants that remove eligibility to win only at the end. These arrangements are not interchangeable: continuing to take normal actions but being unable to win at the end differs from losing all actions partway through play.

The original phase below has a three-round limit, but can end sooner with one eligible participant. Losing the last station triggers departure. Station count and eligibility are recorded separately. Waiting is not converted into unmeasured minutes.
Three rounds of signal competition

Lin, Qiao, and Mu act in that order, with one action slot each per round for three rounds. Their initial station counts are 2, 1, and 2 respectively. Each has 2 batteries and 0 points. Stations are simply pieces in this example. All information is public. Start with an empty removal area and an empty spent-battery area.

An eligible player who still has a station chooses one action: broadcast for 2 points; interfere by first paying 1 battery to the spent area, then removing 1 station belonging to an opponent; or wait without changing anything. An interference target must still be eligible and have at least 1 station. A player cannot target themselves or interfere without paying. Each action removes only one station. There is no other income, trading, borrowing, or station replacement.

Under the original rule, reaching zero stations immediately removes eligibility for this phase. Skip all the player's later slots. They cannot broadcast, interfere, spend resources, or decide for someone else, and receive no final retaliation action. Their earned points remain on the record and unused batteries stay with them, but they cannot win this phase. Removed stations go to their owner's section of the removal area, not to the attacker.

After each action, check eligibility. If only one player remains eligible, end immediately with that player winning; do not finish the three rounds. Otherwise, after three rounds compare points among eligible players. The highest score wins, with tied players sharing the result. Eliminated players do not return during this phase. Once its result is settled, if the group starts another identical trial, everyone rejoins with the initial state. That does not revise the previous result.
Route one: Qiao leaves on the first action
In round one, Lin interferes with Qiao, spending 1 battery. Qiao's only station is removed, eliminating Qiao immediately. Skip Qiao's first-round slot. Mu broadcasts for 2 points.

In round two, Lin broadcasts for 2 points, Qiao's slot is skipped, and Mu spends 1 battery to interfere with Lin. Lin drops from two stations to one and remains in play. In round three, Lin broadcasts for another 2 points, Qiao is skipped, and Mu broadcasts for another 2 points.

Lin and Mu finish on 4 points each and are eligible joint winners. Qiao has 0 points and is ineligible. Stations remaining are 1/0/2, with one Lin station and one Qiao station removed. Batteries remaining are 1/2/1, with 2 spent. All five station pieces and six batteries are accounted for.

Qiao missed three personal action slots. After Qiao's departure, the others made five actual choices: Mu in round one, Lin and Mu in round two, and Lin and Mu in round three. Five choices are not five minutes. How long choices take and how Qiao experiences waiting require separate observation.
Route two: Qiao keeps three actions

Reset the initial state, changing only Lin's first choice to broadcast. Lin still broadcasts in rounds two and three. Mu still broadcasts, interferes with Lin, then broadcasts. Whenever Qiao can take a normal action, Qiao broadcasts.

In round one, each gains 2 points. In round two, Lin and Qiao each gain another 2, while Mu pays 1 battery to remove one of Lin's stations. Everyone broadcasts in round three. Final scores are Lin 6, Qiao 6, and Mu 4, with Lin and Qiao joint winners. Stations remaining are 1/1/2, with only one Lin station removed. Batteries remaining are 2/2/1, with 1 spent.

Qiao never reached zero and received three genuine opportunities to choose. This comparison fixes those choices as broadcasts so the route can be fully resolved. It establishes neither that elimination always helps nor that preserving another player is always better. Different targets, point values, or choices can change the result.
Replace only what happens on the first loss of all stations

Keep route one's action plan, replacing one departure rule: the first time each player reaches zero stations, they keep eligibility and wait for their next personal slot. That slot must return 1 of their own stations from the removal area. It costs no battery but includes no broadcast or interference. Reaching zero again later eliminates them permanently under the original rule. Costs, order, the three-round limit, and victory rules remain unchanged. A player awaiting return has no station and cannot be an interference target.

Lin still removes Qiao's only station in round one. Qiao's next slot returns one station, with points still at 0; Mu broadcasts. In round two, Lin broadcasts, Qiao broadcasts for 2 points, and Mu interferes with Lin. All three broadcast in round three.

Lin, Qiao, and Mu finish with 4 points each and all remain eligible, so they are joint winners. Qiao lost only the first normal choice and could decide what to do in rounds two and three. The first zero-station event is now a temporary loss of an action opportunity, not departure for the entire phase.

If a player's first zero occurs after their last personal slot, no return slot is added. At the end of three rounds, they retain eligibility and compare their existing points. Waiting to return does not extend the phase.
Complete route · Final stations: Lin / Qiao / Mu · Batteries remaining · Recorded points
Qiao eliminated in round one · 1 / 0 / 2 · 1 / 2 / 1 · 4 / 0 / 4
Lin broadcasts first instead · 1 / 1 / 2 · 2 / 2 / 1 · 6 / 6 / 4
Return after the first zero · 1 / 1 / 2 · 1 / 2 / 1 · 4 / 4 / 4

Only Lin's removed station remains out in the return variant. Qiao's station was returned, not created. There are still 2 spent batteries. This rule changes participation after reaching zero and the points available through later slots. The calculation does not establish which arrangement players prefer.
Check: what can this player still do?
Lin drops from two stations to one. Must later actions be skipped? No. Lin still has a station and eligibility. Removing a piece is not itself player elimination.

After original-rule elimination, Qiao still has 2 batteries. Can Qiao spend one to help Mu interfere? No. Retaining material does not preserve action rights. This example has neither transfers nor a final action.
After returning a station in round one, can Qiao immediately broadcast for 2 points? No. Returning used that slot. Qiao's first broadcast is in round two.
If interference leaves only Mu eligible, must play continue until round three ends? No. End immediately with Mu winning. Do not count later slots that have been cancelled.

The core source is Geoffrey Engelstein and Isaac Shalev, Building Blocks of Tabletop Game Design: An Encyclopedia of Mechanisms, second edition, CRC Press, 2022, Chapter 5, VIC-08 “Player Elimination” (EPUB anchor filepos500251). Its complete description and discussion were read. The three-round trial, material, points, action plans, and first-return comparison are original to this site. A round limit is this example's choice, not a necessary property of elimination. Bibliography and DOI

非对称能力：相同资源，哪些行动规则不同？
两名玩家各有 2 能量，不代表他们能完成同样的事情。一个人可能少花一次移动，另一个人可能免付交付费。非对称能力要落实为“谁在什么条件下，可以怎样改变共同规则”，而不只给角色起不同名字。
能力、资源、信息与角色分开看
Geoffrey Engelstein 与 Isaac Shalev 在 ACT-12 “Variable Player Powers”讨论专属行动以及对通常行动、结算程序的修改。本页采用这个能力层面的范围。
仅在开局多放一枚能量，是初始资源差异；只有一人能看到订单，是信息差异；扮演不同角色，则还可能改变目标或叙事身份。这些安排可以与能力并存，但必须分别写出。若两人只是名字不同，能做的行动和费用完全一样，就没有本页要观察的能力差别。
同一条路线上的两位送件员
这是两人原创局部阶段。路线只有三个地点，依次相连：仓库 0—近站 1—远站 2。林与乔都从 0 出发，各带 1 包裹、2 能量，起始 0 分。近站有一份 3 分合同，远站有一份 6 分合同，均公开且各只能完成一次。能量库与已交付区初始为空。
共三轮，每轮林先、乔后，各行动一次。通常行动为：移动到相邻地点，付 1 能量；在有未完成合同的近站或远站送达，付 1 能量并交出本人 1 包裹，取得合同分；或等待，不付费也不产生效果。费用先支付，包裹进已交付区，合同移到完成者面前。费用、包裹或合同不足就不能送达。
可以同处一地，不能交易、借能量或重新拿包裹。移动与送达是两种行动：到达或经过站点不会自动完成合同。所有支付的能量进入能量库，不补充到玩家手中。第三轮两人都行动完才结束，合同提前完成也不增加或取消名额。比较已获合同分，最高者胜，同分并列；剩余能量、包裹和位置不计分。
两项能力从开始就公开，归属固定：林的“跨步”每阶段可用一次，把一次移动变成沿线连续走两边，不能折返，仍付 1 能量；只有走满两边才使用这项能力，先付费并标记用过，再移动。乔的“免交付费”把本人的送达能量费从 1 改为 0；仍需花一次行动、交出包裹并取得未完成合同，移动费照付。
因此林可以用跨步从 0 到 2，却不能无限次跨步；乔可以没能量时送达，却不能没包裹时送达。两人不能使用对方的能力。
过程一：林去远站，乔去近站
第一轮林跨步到 2，付 1 能量，剩 1；乔普通移动到 1，付 1，剩 1。林经过近站没有取合同，两份合同都还在。
第二轮林先付最后 1 能量，交包裹完成远站合同，得 6 分；乔以自己的能力免能量费，交包裹完成近站合同，得 3 分。第三轮两人等待。
结束时林在 2、乔在 1，能量为 0／1，包裹都已交出，能量库有 3，已交付区有 2 包裹；两份合同分属林、乔。林以 6 比 3 获胜。跨步用一次行动走完了远路，免交付费让乔留下了一枚能量，但剩余能量在本阶段并不加分。
过程二：近站先被林完成
回到相同初始状态。第一轮林与乔都普通移动到 1，各付 1 能量，剩 1。两人可以同处近站；林尚未用跨步。
第二轮林先付最后 1 能量，交包裹取得近站 3 分合同。乔不能再交同一份合同，于是花最后 1 能量普通移动到 2。第三轮林等待，乔虽然为 0 能量，仍能用免交付费交出包裹，取得远站 6 分合同。
结束时林在 1、乔在 2，两人能量与包裹都为 0；能量库有 4，已交付区有 2 包裹。乔以 6 比 3 获胜。林的跨步能力尚未使用，不能因此自动补一份奖励。两条过程显示能力何时能发挥作用，没有证明两个角色整体平衡。
只提高林跨步的费用
现在只把跨步的能量费从 1 改为 2，普通移动与乔的能力不变。沿用过程一的计划：林先跨步到远站，第二轮若能合法送达就送达，否则等待，第三轮等待；乔仍移动近站、送达、等待。这个“付不起则等待”的选择在比较两版时相同。
第一轮林能支付 2 能量完成跨步，但到站后能量为 0。第二轮他没有送达所需的 1 能量，因此选择等待，既不交包裹也不得分。乔仍以免交付费完成近站合同，得 3 分；最后两人等待。
完整过程 · 剩余能量：林／乔 · 剩余包裹 · 合同分
跨步改付 2，沿用第一计划 · 0 / 1 · 1 / 0 · 0 / 3
改价版能量库仍有 3，已交付区只有乔的 1 包裹；林还携带 1 包裹，远站合同未完成。地图位置与过程一相同，结果却不同，因为到达位置与能否支付下一步费用是两件事。
这个对照只识别跨步费用在当前预算、行动次数和合同下的后果。若要判断平衡，还需改变先手、任务距离、奖励、资源以及对手选择，并观察实际玩法，不能把一次胜负或两次分数交换当成证明。
自查：能力到底免除了什么？
乔在远站有 0 能量、1 包裹，远站合同还在，能送达吗？能。免掉的是送达的能量费；交出包裹、使用行动和合同可领取这三项条件仍要满足。不会倒赚 1 能量。
林刚取走近站合同，乔在同一地点也能交包裹拿 3 分吗？不能。合同只有一份，已经完成。同格不代表有第二份合同。
林用过跨步后还剩 1 能量，可以再次从 2 跨回 0 吗？不能。付得起费用不等于还有使用次数；林仍可选择合法的普通移动。
两人三轮都等待，谁获胜？两人均为 0 分，按规则并列；各保留 2 能量、1 包裹，公共合同都未完成。
来源与范围

核心来源为 Geoffrey Engelstein 与 Isaac Shalev，Building Blocks of Tabletop Game Design: An Encyclopedia of Mechanisms，第二版，CRC Press，2022，第 3 章 ACT-12 “Variable Player Powers”（EPUB 锚点 filepos263056）。已读完整描述与讨论；路线、合同、预算、两种能力、行动计划与费用对照均为本站原创。书目与 DOI

Asymmetric powers: with equal resources, which action rules differ?

Two players with 2 energy each need not be able to accomplish the same things. One might save a movement action; another might waive a delivery fee. An asymmetric power needs to specify who may change a shared rule, how, and under what conditions, beyond giving characters different names.
Separate powers, resources, information, and roles

In ACT-12, “Variable Player Powers,” Geoffrey Engelstein and Isaac Shalev discuss exclusive actions and changes to ordinary actions or resolution procedures. This entry focuses on that ability-level scope.

Placing one additional energy at setup is an initial-resource difference. Letting only one player see an order is an information difference. Different roles can also change objectives or narrative identity. These arrangements can coexist with powers, but should be specified separately. If only the names differ while available actions and costs are identical, there is no power difference of the kind examined here.
Two couriers on one route

This is an original local phase for two players. There are three locations in a line: warehouse 0—near station 1—far station 2. Lin and Qiao both start at 0 with 1 parcel, 2 energy, and 0 points each. The near station has one public 3-point contract, and the far station one public 6-point contract. Each can be completed only once. The energy bank and delivered-parcel area begin empty.

There are three rounds. Lin takes one action before Qiao in each round. Ordinary actions are: move to an adjacent location for 1 energy; deliver at the near or far station with an uncompleted contract by paying 1 energy and surrendering 1 personal parcel, gaining the contract's points; or wait at no cost and with no effect. Pay first, place the parcel in the delivered area, and move the contract in front of its completer. Delivery is illegal without the fee, parcel, or available contract.

Players may share a location. There is no trading, borrowing energy, or obtaining another parcel. Moving and delivering are separate actions: arriving at or passing a station does not complete a contract. All spent energy enters the bank and is not replenished into players' supplies. Finish after both actions in round three, even if contracts were completed earlier; this neither adds nor cancels slots. The highest contract-point total wins, with ties shared. Remaining energy, parcels, and position score nothing.

Both powers are public from the start and remain with their owners. Lin's “Long Stride” can be used once per phase to move two consecutive edges along the line in one movement action, without reversing direction, still paying 1 energy. Moving the full two edges uses the power: pay and mark it used before moving. Qiao's “Delivery Fee Waiver” changes the energy cost of Qiao's delivery from 1 to 0. It still requires an action, a parcel, and an uncompleted contract. Movement costs remain unchanged.
Lin can therefore stride from 0 to 2, but cannot do so indefinitely. Qiao can deliver with no energy, but not with no parcel. Neither can use the other's power.
Route one: Lin goes far, Qiao goes near

In round one, Lin strides to 2, paying 1 energy and retaining 1. Qiao moves normally to 1, also paying 1 and retaining 1. Passing the near station did not give Lin its contract; both remain available.

In round two, Lin pays the last 1 energy and hands over the parcel to complete the far contract for 6 points. Qiao uses the waiver to deliver the parcel at no energy cost, completing the near contract for 3 points. Both wait in round three.

Lin finishes at 2 and Qiao at 1, with energy 0/1 and both parcels delivered. The bank holds 3 energy and the delivered area 2 parcels; the contracts belong to Lin and Qiao respectively. Lin wins 6 to 3. The stride covered the far route in one action; the waiver left Qiao one energy, but remaining energy does not score in this phase.
Route two: Lin completes the near contract first
Return to the same initial state. In round one, both move normally to 1, paying 1 energy each and retaining 1. They may share the near station. Lin has not used the stride.

In round two, Lin pays the last 1 energy and delivers the parcel for the near contract's 3 points. Qiao cannot complete that same contract again, so spends the last 1 energy to move normally to 2. Lin waits in round three. Despite having 0 energy, Qiao can use the waiver to deliver the parcel for the far contract's 6 points.

Lin finishes at 1 and Qiao at 2. Both have 0 energy and no parcel; the bank holds 4 energy and the delivered area 2 parcels. Qiao wins 6 to 3. Lin's unused stride grants no automatic bonus. The two routes show conditions in which each power matters; they do not establish overall balance between the characters.
Raise only the price of Lin's stride

Now change only the stride's energy cost from 1 to 2. Ordinary movement and Qiao's power remain unchanged. Keep route one's plan: Lin strides to the far station, delivers in round two if legal and otherwise waits, then waits in round three. Qiao still moves to the near station, delivers, and waits. The “wait if delivery is unaffordable” choice is the same in both versions.

In round one, Lin can pay 2 energy to stride, but arrives with 0. In round two, Lin lacks the 1 energy required for delivery and chooses to wait, retaining the parcel and gaining no points. Qiao still waives the fee and completes the near contract for 3 points. Both wait in the final round.
Complete route · Energy remaining: Lin / Qiao · Parcels remaining · Contract points
Lin far, Qiao near · 0 / 1 · 0 / 0 · 6 / 3
Lin near, Qiao far · 0 / 0 · 0 / 0 · 3 / 6
Stride costs 2, first plan retained · 0 / 1 · 1 / 0 · 0 / 3

In the changed-price version, the bank still holds 3 energy, but the delivered area contains only Qiao's 1 parcel. Lin retains 1 parcel, and the far contract remains uncompleted. Positions match route one, but the result differs: reaching a location and being able to pay for the next action are separate conditions.

This comparison identifies the stride fee's consequences only under these budgets, action counts, and contracts. Assessing balance would require changing initiative, distances, rewards, resources, and opposing choices, alongside observing actual play. One win or an exchange of scores is not proof.
Check: what exactly does the power waive?

Qiao is at the far station with 0 energy and 1 parcel, and its contract remains available. Is delivery legal? Yes. The energy fee is waived. The parcel, action, and available-contract requirements remain. Qiao does not gain 1 energy as a refund.

Lin has just taken the near contract. Can Qiao, at the same location, deliver for another 3 points? No. There was one contract and it is completed. Sharing a location does not create another contract.
After using the stride, Lin still has 1 energy. Can Lin stride back from 2 to 0? No. Affording the fee does not restore a use. Lin may still choose a legal ordinary move.
Who wins if both wait in all three rounds? Both score 0 and tie. Each retains 2 energy and 1 parcel, and both public contracts remain uncompleted.

团队结构：一起赢，分别决定什么
团队结构先回答胜利归谁：一组玩家作为队伍，与其他队伍竞争。但“我们一起赢”还没有说明谁能决定行动、谁能花资源、谁能知道队友的选择。这些规则共同决定合作是在商量、分工，还是在有限线索下配合。
《Building Blocks of Tabletop Game Design》第二版 STR-03 将团队对抗列为一种游戏结构，并讨论组队、交流权限和角色分工；资源共享只是可能采用的安排。以下“分路运输”是本站原创的局部教学游戏，用一轮完整结算拆开这些问题，不对应任何商业游戏，也不是完整对局历史。
一轮运输的完整规则
四人分成公开且固定的两队：红队的林任导航员、乔任装载员；蓝队的韩任导航员、岳任装载员。每位导航员各有“北路、南路”两张路线牌；每位装载员各有“北装具、南装具、不装载”三张选择牌和 2 枚能量。共 10 张选择牌、4 枚能量，银行起初没有能量，没有其他资源或随机事件。
所有人知道规则、初始资源和队伍。准备结束后不得交谈、示意或展示牌。每人只能选择自己的牌，不能代替队友决定，也不能转移、借用能量。具体顺序如下。
两位导航员各自秘密选一张路线牌，同时锁定；只有本人知道所选路线，此后不能改。
两位装载员各自秘密选一张牌并锁定。北装具费用为 2 能量，南装具为 1，不装载为 0；必须能用自己的能量付清。费用先不支付，以免金额泄露选择，且此时没有其他行动或资源变化。
四人同时翻牌，两位装载员立即向银行支付完整费用。即使装具与路线不配，也照常付费，不退款。
路线与装具同为北或同为南，该队才有资格分取对应路线的奖励；不装载从不取得资格。北路有 8 队伍分，南路有 6 队伍分。某路只有一队合格，该队全拿；两队都合格，平分该路奖励；无人合格，该路奖励不发。
每队再把本队装载员剩余的能量按每枚 1 分加入队伍总分。分高的一队两人共同获胜；同分则两队、四人平局。随即结束，没有追加行动、个人排名或额外奖励。
没有资格的队伍不参与分奖，也不会挤占另一队的奖励。能量只是从装载员流向银行，4 枚总量不变；分数是结算生成的，不是支付货币。
两条完整过程：失配损失由谁承担
下面两条过程都合法，固定林选北路、韩选南路、岳选南装具，只改变乔的实际选择。基础规则下乔看不到林的牌，因此第一条不能理解成乔已经知道正确答案。
过程 · 红队结算 · 蓝队结算 · 结束结果
配合成功：乔选北装具 · 北路配北装具，付 2；独得北路 8 分，余 0，合计 8 · 南路配南装具，付 1；独得南路 6 分，余 1，合计 7 · 红队两人获胜；银行 3，乔 0，岳 1
配合失配：乔选南装具 · 北路配南装具，付 1；无路线奖励，余 1，合计 1 · 南路配南装具，付 1；红队不合格，蓝队仍独得 6 分，余 1，合计 7 · 蓝队两人获胜；银行 2，乔 1，岳 1
失配时，乔买了南装具，并不让红队自动改走南路。导航员锁定路线的决定权与装载员选装具的决定权是两件事。乔少花的 1 能量也没有补回失去的 8 分路线奖励；这个具体选择让红队总分从 8 变为 1。
损失写在队伍分上，林与乔共同承担。规则没有依据“是谁选错”再分出一位个人输家，也没有让获胜蓝队中的岳因为保留了能量而比韩更胜一筹。团队归属改变的是结果归属，不会自动合并每个人的操作权限。
只改一条规则：让队友提前看到路线
改版仅在两位导航员锁定之后、装载员选择之前，把各自的路线展示给本队装载员。对手仍不能看，仍不得交谈；路线不能修改，装载员仍自己决定、自己付费，奖励和胜负规则完全相同。
为了比较信息本身，给两位装载员固定同一决策方法：“若能看到己方路线，就选匹配装具；否则选南装具。”仍令林锁北、韩锁南。基础版中，两人都选南装具，得到上一表的红 1、蓝 7；改版中，乔看见北路而选北装具，岳仍选南装具，得到红 8、蓝 7。两版能量支付分别为 2 与 3，没有免费补偿。
提前披露让这套方法能完成配合，却没有把乔的行动交给林。乔依然可以合法地选不匹配装具或不装载。两队也可能都用匹配装具走北路而各得 4 分；看到队友的路线不会告诉自己对手去了哪里，更不保证独占奖励。若等到全部翻牌后才允许看路线，已经错过选择窗口，不能倒回去重选。
适用处与边界
当设计希望玩家拥有不同职责，却共享一场竞争的结果时，团队结构很有用。可以分别检查：队伍怎样形成、何时能交流、谁有最终决定权、资源能否转移、奖励记到个人还是队伍。本站从算例得到的设计判断是，先确定这些权限，再判断一次失配究竟来自信息不足、决定冲突还是资源安排；只写“请大家合作”无法区分原因。
团队不必人数相等，也不必采用固定队伍；本例的公开双人队只是其中一种。全桌共同对抗系统时，胜负覆盖全体玩家，可继续看合作结构。隐藏信息描述谁知道什么，既可出现在队内，也可出现在队间。叛徒结构还涉及不一致的阵营目标，不能仅凭队友暂时看不到路线就推断存在背叛。相应条目可从下方关联入口继续阅读。
限制交流可能增加每位队员的判断空间，也可能让失配显得任意；允许讨论可能便于协作，也可能令一位熟练玩家包办意见。这些是需要观察的体验，团队标签本身不能保证参与感或公平。
自查与答案
两队都选北路和北装具，会怎样？ 两队各付 2，北路奖励平分，各得 4 分且没有剩余能量。银行有 4，双方平局，不能让先翻牌的一队优先拿 8 分。
两队都选南路和南装具呢？ 两队各付 1，各分到南路 3 分，再加剩余能量 1 分，仍是 4 比 4；银行 2，两位装载员各余 1。
两队导航员都选北，乔不装载，岳选北装具，北路奖励要平分吗？ 不。红队不合格，保留 2 能量得 2 分；蓝队独得 8 分、余 0，蓝队获胜，银行有 2。
若乔只有 1 能量，另 1 枚已在银行，岳仍有 2，林能替乔决定购买北装具吗？ 不能。北装具需要乔本人持有 2 能量，也只能由乔选择；看见路线、同队或全桌总量足够，都没有新增借用与代付权限。
来源与进一步阅读

核心依据为 Geoffrey Engelstein 与 Isaac Shalev 的 《Building Blocks of Tabletop Game Design》第二版（2022），STR-03 “Team-Based Games”，印刷页 8–11，讨论团队竞争、交流与分工；STR-02 “Cooperative Games”，印刷页 4–7，讨论共同目标与个体行动决定。本文的运输规则、比较数值和设计判断均为本站原创推演。

Team structure: winning together, deciding separately

A team structure first answers who receives victory: a group of players competes against other groups as a team. “We win together” still leaves open who chooses actions, who spends resources, and who knows a partner’s choice. Those rules determine whether cooperation involves discussion, divided responsibilities, or coordination with limited clues.

STR-03 in the second edition of Building Blocks of Tabletop Game Design treats competition between teams as a game structure and discusses team formation, communication, and differentiated roles. Sharing resources is one possible arrangement. The one-round transport game below is an original teaching example that separates these questions. It does not reproduce a commercial game or a complete play history.
Complete rules for one delivery round

Four players form two public, fixed teams. Red has Lin as navigator and Qiao as loader; Blue has Han as navigator and Yue as loader. Each navigator holds two route cards, North and South. Each loader holds three choice cards, North Kit, South Kit, and No Load, plus 2 energy tokens. There are 10 choice cards and 4 energy tokens in total. The bank starts empty. There are no other resources or random events.

Everyone knows the rules, starting resources, and teams. After setup, players may not talk, signal, or show cards. Each player chooses only their own card, cannot make a partner’s decision, and cannot transfer or borrow energy. Resolve the following sequence.
Both navigators secretly select and simultaneously lock one route card. Only its owner knows the choice, which can no longer change.

Both loaders secretly select and lock one card. North Kit costs 2 energy, South Kit costs 1, and No Load costs 0. A loader must be able to pay the full cost from their own energy. Payment waits until the reveal so its amount does not disclose the choice. No other actions or resource changes occur in this interval.
All four players reveal together. Loaders immediately pay their full costs to the bank, including for a mismatched kit. There are no refunds.

A team qualifies for a route’s reward only if its route and kit both name North or both name South. No Load never qualifies. North awards 8 team points and South awards 6. One qualifying team takes the whole reward; two qualifying teams split that route’s reward equally; a route with no qualifying team awards nothing.

Each team adds 1 team point per energy token its loader has left. Both members of the higher-scoring team win together. Equal totals mean a draw for both teams and all four players. The game ends immediately, with no further actions, individual ranking, or additional rewards.

An unqualified team does not share or reduce another team’s reward. Energy moves only from loaders to the bank, conserving all 4 tokens. Points are generated during scoring; they are not payment currency.
Two complete outcomes: who bears a mismatch?

Both sequences below are legal. Keep Lin on North, Han on South, and Yue on South Kit; change only Qiao’s actual choice. Under the base rules Qiao cannot see Lin’s card, so the first sequence does not mean Qiao already knew the correct answer.
Sequence · Red’s settlement · Blue’s settlement · Final result

Successful coordination: Qiao picks North Kit · North matches North Kit; pay 2, receive all 8 North points, retain 0 energy: total 8 · South matches South Kit; pay 1, receive all 6 South points, retain 1 energy: total 7 · Both Red players win; bank 3, Qiao 0, Yue 1

Mismatch: Qiao picks South Kit · North does not match South Kit; pay 1, receive no route reward, retain 1 energy: total 1 · South matches South Kit; pay 1. Red is unqualified, so Blue still receives all 6 points and retains 1 energy: total 7 · Both Blue players win; bank 2, Qiao 1, Yue 1

Buying South Kit does not automatically reroute Red to South. Authority to lock a route and authority to choose a kit are separate. Saving 1 energy does not replace the lost 8-point route reward: this particular choice lowers Red’s total from 8 to 1.

The loss appears in the team score, and Lin and Qiao share it. The rules do not assign a separate individual defeat according to who made the mistake. Nor does Yue win more than Han because Yue retained energy. Team membership determines who shares the result; it does not automatically merge everyone’s action permissions.
Change one rule: show a partner the route earlier

In the variant, after both navigators lock their routes but before loaders choose, each navigator shows the locked route only to their own loader. Opponents still cannot see it, and discussion remains forbidden. Routes cannot change. Loaders still make their own choices and pay their own costs. Rewards and victory conditions remain identical.

To compare the information itself, give both loaders the same fixed decision policy: “If my team’s route is visible to me, choose its matching kit; otherwise choose South Kit.” Again, Lin locks North and Han locks South. In the base version both loaders choose South Kit, producing Red 1 and Blue 7. In the variant Qiao sees North and chooses North Kit, while Yue still chooses South Kit, producing Red 8 and Blue 7. Total energy payments are 2 and 3 respectively; there is no free compensation.

Earlier disclosure lets this policy coordinate successfully, but does not give Lin control of Qiao’s action. Qiao may still legally choose a mismatched kit or No Load. Both teams might also match North with North Kit and receive 4 points each. Seeing a partner’s route reveals nothing about the opposing route and does not guarantee an exclusive reward. Permission to see the route only after everyone reveals comes too late to change a choice.
Uses and boundaries

Team structures are useful when players should hold different responsibilities while sharing the outcome of a competition. Check separately how teams form, when communication is allowed, who makes each final decision, whether resources can move, and whether rewards belong to individuals or teams. Our inference from the example is that these permissions help identify whether a mismatch comes from missing information, conflicting decisions, or resource arrangements. Simply asking players to cooperate cannot distinguish those causes.

Teams need not be equal in size or fixed throughout play. Public pairs are only one arrangement. When the whole table competes against a system, the result covers every player; the cooperative-structure entry develops that case. Hidden information concerns who knows what and can occur within or between teams. A traitor structure also involves conflicting faction objectives: temporarily hiding a route from a teammate does not establish betrayal. Continue through the related entries below.

Limiting communication may give each player more judgment to exercise, or make mismatches feel arbitrary. Discussion may help coordination, or allow an experienced player to dominate recommendations. These are experiences to observe; a team label alone guarantees neither participation nor fairness.
Self-checks and answers

What if both teams choose North and North Kit? Each pays 2 and receives half of North’s reward: 4 points, with no energy left. The bank holds 4 and the teams draw. Revealing first does not grant priority over the full 8-point reward.
What if both choose South and South Kit? Each pays 1, receives 3 route points, and adds 1 for retained energy: another 4–4 draw. The bank holds 2 and each loader retains 1.

Both navigators choose North, Qiao chooses No Load, and Yue chooses North Kit. Must they split North’s reward? No. Red is unqualified and scores 2 from retained energy. Blue receives all 8 points and retains 0 energy. Blue wins; the bank holds 2.

Suppose Qiao has only 1 energy, the other token is already in the bank, and Yue still has 2. Can Lin choose to buy North Kit for Qiao? No. Qiao must personally hold 2 energy to choose North Kit and must make that choice. Seeing the route, sharing a team, or having enough energy across the table creates no borrowing or payment permission.
Sources and further reading

The core source is Geoffrey Engelstein and Isaac Shalev’s Building Blocks of Tabletop Game Design, second edition (2022), STR-03, “Team-Based Games,” printed pages 8–11, on team competition, communication, and differentiated roles; and STR-02, “Cooperative Games,” printed pages 4–7, on shared objectives and individual action decisions.
